tutos.configOs.title: OS Setup
tutos.configOs.intro: Before connecting with ChillShell, your PC needs to accept SSH connections. Follow the steps for your operating system.
tutos.configOs.win.step1.title: Install OpenSSH
tutos.configOs.win.step1.content: OpenSSH lets your PC accept remote connections from ChillShell. You need both the Client and the Server.
tutos.configOs.win.step1.warning: You must always install OpenSSH Client BEFORE OpenSSH Server. The Client is often already installed by default on Windows — if you don't see it in the available features, it's already active and you can go straight to the Server.
tutos.configOs.win.step1.graphical.step1: Open Windows Settings, then go to System > Optional features.
tutos.configOs.win.step1.graphical.step4: In the search bar, type "open". If OpenSSH Client appears, add it FIRST on its own and wait for it to finish. Then add OpenSSH Server. If only OpenSSH Server appears, the Client is already installed — just add the Server.
tutos.configOs.win.step1.graphical.clien: Never check both at the same time. Always Client first, then Server after.
tutos.configOs.win.step1.graphical.resta: Restart your PC for the installation to take effect.

tutos.tailscale.title: Tailscale VPN
tutos.tailscale.intro: Tailscale lets you connect to your PC from anywhere — WiFi, 5G, abroad. No port forwarding needed.
tutos.tailscale.step1.title: Install Tailscale on your PC
tutos.tailscale.win.step1.content: Download from tailscale.com and install. Sign in with your Google/Microsoft/GitHub account.
tutos.tailscale.linux.step1.code:
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up
tutos.tailscale.mac.step1.content: Download from the Mac App Store or tailscale.com. Sign in with the same account.
tutos.tailscale.step2.title: Install on your phone
tutos.tailscale.step2.content: Download Tailscale from Play Store or App Store. Sign in with the same account you used on your PC.
tutos.tailscale.step3.title: Get your Tailscale IP
tutos.tailscale.step3.content: Open Tailscale on your PC. Your IP starts with 100.x.x.x. Use this IP in ChillShell instead of your local IP.
tutos.tailscale.step4.title: Connect with ChillShell
tutos.tailscale.step4.content: In ChillShell, create a new session with your Tailscale IP (100.x.x.x) and your username. It works everywhere: WiFi, 5G, abroad.
tutos.bios.title: BIOS Setup (Wake-on-LAN)
tutos.bios.intro: To use Wake-on-LAN, your BIOS needs specific settings enabled. The exact names vary by brand, but here's what to look for.
tutos.bios.generic.title: What to look for
tutos.bios.generic.content: Look for these settings (names vary by brand): "Wake on LAN", "Power On By PCI-E", "ErP Ready" (must be Disabled), "Resume by LAN", "Wake Up on LAN".
tutos.bios.asus.title: ASUS / ROG
tutos.bios.asus.content:
1. Enter BIOS (press DEL at boot)
2. Advanced Mode (F7)
3. Advanced > APM Configuration
4. Set "ErP Ready" to Disabled
5. Set "Power On By PCI-E" to Enabled
6. If issues persist: Advanced > Onboard Devices > set ASPM to Disabled
7. Save & Exit (F10)
tutos.wol.title: Wake-on-LAN
tutos.wol.intro: Wake-on-LAN lets you power on your PC remotely from ChillShell.
tutos.wol.warning: Important: Wake-on-LAN only works on the local network via Ethernet cable. WiFi is not supported.
tutos.wol.step1.title: Enable in BIOS
tutos.wol.step1.content: See the BIOS Setup tutorial to enable the required settings.
tutos.wol.win.step2.title: Enable in Windows
tutos.wol.win.step2.intro: Open Device Manager and find your Ethernet adapter under Network adapters.
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub1.title: Advanced tab: Wake on Magic Packet
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub1.content: Right-click your Ethernet adapter > Properties > Advanced tab. Find "Wake on Magic Packet" and set it to Enabled.
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub2.title: Power Management tab
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub2.content: Go to the Power Management tab. Check "Allow this device to wake the computer" and "Only allow a magic packet to wake the computer".
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub3.title: Disable Fast Startup
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub3.content: Fast Startup can prevent Wake-on-LAN from working. To disable it: Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Uncheck "Turn on fast startup".
tutos.wol.win.step2.powershellCode:
# Check which devices can wake the PC
powercfg /devicequery wake_armed

# Disable Fast Startup via registry
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power" /v HiberbootEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
tutos.wol.win.step3.graphicalContent: Open Settings > Network & Internet > Ethernet. Scroll down to find your physical (MAC) address.
tutos.wol.linux.step2.title: Enable in Linux
tutos.wol.linux.step2.persist: To make it persistent, add a systemd service or use NetworkManager.

security.title: Security
security.simple.keys: Your SSH keys stay on your phone. Never sent anywhere.
security.simple.pin: PIN hashed, never stored in plaintext
security.simple.noData: No data transmitted to our servers
security.detail.storage.title: Data storage
security.detail.storage.content: SSH keys and credentials are stored using flutter_secure_storage: AES-CBC on Android (EncryptedSharedPreferences), Keychain on iOS. Master key stored in hardware-backed keystore.
security.detail.ssh.title: SSH connection
security.detail.ssh.content: Trust On First Use (TOFU) for host verification. Ed25519 preferred. Keys loaded into memory only during active session, then securely disposed via SecureBuffer.
security.detail.auth.title: Local authentication
security.detail.auth.content: PIN hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 100k iterations. Biometric unlock via local_auth. Auto-lock after inactivity.
security.detail.leaks.title: Leak protection
security.detail.leaks.content: Command history filtered with regex. Clipboard auto-cleanup. FLAG_SECURE on Android prevents screenshots.
security.detail.root.title: Root/jailbreak detection
security.detail.root.content: Common root paths verified at launch. Warning banner shown if detected. App remains functional.
security.detail.audit.title: Audit log
security.detail.audit.content: Security events logged locally. FIFO rotation at 500 entries. Events: login, session start/end, key generation.
security.detail.limits.title: Known limitations
security.detail.limits.content: SecureBuffer cannot guarantee GC won't copy data. Root detection is bypassable on rooted devices. These are documented for full transparency.
security.detail.scores.title: Audit results
security.detail.scores.content: White-box audit: 8.5/10. STRIDE threat model: 100% mitigated. Full reports available on request.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Which server OS does ChillShell work with?
faq.a1: Any OS with an SSH server: Windows (with OpenSSH), Linux, macOS. See our OS Setup tutorial.
faq.q2: Does it work with Claude Code / Cursor CLI / Codex?
faq.a2: Yes! ChillShell supports all CLI agents via SSH. Check our CLI Agents page for the full compatibility table.
faq.a3: No. Wake-on-LAN requires an Ethernet cable connection. Your phone must also be on the same local network.
faq.q4: Can I use ChillShell without Wake-on-LAN?
faq.a4: Absolutely. WoL is optional. You can use ChillShell purely for SSH connections — locally or via Tailscale.
faq.a5: No. All data stays on your phone. We don't collect anything. See our Security page for details.
faq.q6: Is the payment one-time or recurring?
faq.a6: One-time purchase. $2.99 for lifetime access. No subscription, no hidden fees.
faq.a7: Refunds follow Google Play and App Store policies. Contact us within the refund window of your platform.
